beats.idea: Purchasing power, gold backing and legal status questioned
beats.shows: Note–rice, gold, payment–law pairs with question marks
beats.template_note: Payment and buying are questions here, not demonstrated transactions. Reveal note–rice first, gold with a question mark on 'gold', then payment acceptance versus a stamped law scroll on 'कानून'; retain question marks without ticks or answers.

beats.idea: Gold-backed note redeemable; today's rupee is not
beats.relation_note: Contrast historical hypothetical gold redemption with today's rupee using matching bank-and-holder slots.
beats.shows: Old note becomes gold; modern redemption crossed out
beats.template_note: Holder returns one hypothetical note; teller receives it and hands back gold labelled 1 gram. Gold remains in holder's hand. On 'नहीं', cross the modern rupee-to-gold redemption arrow, not the rupee note.

beats.idea: Value comes from gold redemption, not paper
beats.shows: Note exchanged for gold; paper beside goods receipt
beats.template_note: Holder presents note; clerk takes it and hands over a fixed quantity of gold. Then contrast paper material with its claim, using a receipt linked to goods.

beats.idea: Gold holdings alone do not establish redemption rights
beats.shows: Identical gold vaults; only one note carries claim
beats.template_note: Having gold and holding a claim are conditions being compared, not a narrated transaction.

beats.idea: New notes carry additional redemption promises
beats.shows: New notes → redemption claims → gold backing
beats.template_note: This previews a causal explanation, not an issuance or redemption transaction.

beats.idea: Extra note needs extra gold backing
beats.shows: Ten gold-note pairs; extra gold enables eleventh note
beats.template_note: Show an eleventh note with a question mark; build ten numbered notes paired with ten 1g gold units, each note bearing a 1g promise. Add another 1g gold unit to the bank reserve, then connect it to the eleventh note and reveal a tick.

beats.idea: Gold reserves back the redemption promise
beats.shows: Vault gold linked to note’s promise slip
beats.template_note: Defines backing and reserves; no transfer occurs.

beats.idea: Gold backing constrains issuance and supports redemption
beats.shows: Vault backs issuance; notes return for gold
beats.template_note: First bank hands out notes backed by vault gold; then holder hands notes back and receives fixed gold. Keep a conditions gate at redemption, labelled 'in principle; unrestricted नहीं'. Do not depict automatic one-for-one reserve quantities.

beats.idea: Weaker repayment capacity triggers gold demands
beats.shows: Reserves shrink; trust breaks; holders demand gold
beats.template_note: Shrink reserves against unchanged claims, break the trust link, then move holders with notes toward the counter demanding gold; do not show completed redemption.

beats.idea: Promise, reserves and constrained issuance form a chain
beats.shows: Promise → gold reserves → bound note issuance
beats.template_note: Conceptual recap, not a new transaction. Attach '1 gram: सिर्फ उदाहरण' to a small gold example, outside the main chain.

beats.idea: Issuing notes carries redemption responsibility
beats.shows: Issued note tethered to bank’s redemption promise
beats.template_note: Summarizes the obligation behind issuance rather than performing another redemption.

book_pictures.title: A horizontal line links four chronological dots
A horizontal timeline connects four dots from left to right

beats.idea: Receipts introduce paper claims
beats.shows: Goods beside receipt; question mark beside receipt
beats.template_note: Hypothetical substitution introduces the question, not an enacted transaction.

beats.idea: Deposited value gains a state-issued claim
beats.shows: Stored valuables underpin receipt; state seal marks note
beats.template_note: Shows evidence of value and issuer identity, not a deposit or issuance process.

beats.idea: Compulsory acceptance predates Sweden's banknotes
beats.shows: Refusal cross; stamped law beside note; Sweden later
beats.template_note: Recipient first refuses the note; at compulsory, replace the hypothetical refusal with the binding law beside it. Highlight 1275 before 1661.

beats.idea: Gold links differ across monetary arrangements
beats.shows: Money–gold versus official dollar–gold; public counter crossed
beats.template_note: Compare monetary arrangements without inventing an individual redemption transaction.

beats.idea: Gold redemption ends at the shared endpoint
beats.shows: Dollar–gold link breaks; both 1971 endpoints converge
beats.template_note: Break the redemption connector, then join both historical timelines at their 1971 fiat endpoints.

beats.idea: Why accept money without gold redemption?
beats.shows: Crossed gold promise; recipient questions paper note
beats.template_note: Acceptance is being questioned, not demonstrated or answered yet.

beats.idea: Issuer, acceptance and backing evolve
beats.shows: Receipt, issuer seal, acceptance law, gold, fiat
beats.template_note: Recap the historical milestones by highlighting existing icons, without adding an acceptance transaction.

beats.idea: Acceptance rests on trust in future spending
beats.shows: Rice exchanged; note accepted; onward spending imagined
beats.template_note: At क्यों, show a question mark beside the note. Buyer hands ₹100 to shopkeeper and receives rice. At स्वीकार, shopkeeper nods and a tick appears on the note. At आगे, a thought bubble shows the shopkeeper spending that same note with another seller, who accepts it for goods.

beats.idea: Authority and trust give fiat purchasing power
beats.shows: Authority and trust support note; tomorrow buys groceries
beats.template_note: Authority seal and trusting public point to note value; cross out paper material as its source. Advance calendar from today to tomorrow; holder pays note and shopkeeper gives groceries.

beats.idea: Gold redemption differs from fiat backing
beats.shows: Gold redemption beside authority-and-trust-backed fiat note
beats.template_note: In the gold-backed panel, holder returns paper at counter and receives gold; the fiat panel instead retains authority and public-trust symbols. Do not label all paper notes fiat.

beats.idea: How is issuance controlled without gold?
beats.shows: Authority, trust, note stack; control question without gold
beats.template_note: Issue control is only posed as a forthcoming question; its process is not explained here.

book_pictures.title: Major Examples of Fiat Currency Today

beats.idea: Fiat value rests on authority and trust
beats.shows: Press versus issuance; authority supports paper and digits
beats.template_note: Printing and issuance are posed as a distinction; their process follows next beat.

beats.idea: Printing is not net money creation
beats.shows: Printed notes await authorisation; replacement totals stay equal
beats.template_note: Press produces notes; authorisation opens circulation gate; equal old and new batches exchange without increasing total.

beats.idea: Credit conditions affect demand with delays
beats.shows: Costlier loans slow expansion, spending and price pressure
beats.template_note: Policy and liquidity controls raise loan cost; expansion pauses, borrowing and spending shrink, pressure eases after clock delay; cheaper-credit arrows reverse, goods shelf unchanged.

beats.idea: Codes identify dollar and shared euro
beats.shows: USD links America; EUR links multiple EU countries

beats.idea: Same yen symbol, different currency codes
beats.shows: Identical ¥ tags split into JPY and CNY
beats.template_note: Trade and reserves describe currency roles, not a specific payment process.

beats.idea: Old currency name does not mean continuous fiat
beats.shows: GBP timeline separates ancient roots from fiat status
beats.template_note: Historical continuity is illustrated without inventing intermediate dates or redemption terms.

beats.idea: Historical euro adopters are a subset
beats.shows: Twenty highlighted tiles within twenty-seven; historical badge
beats.template_note: Build 27 anonymous member tiles, highlight 20 and leave seven unhighlighted; mark historical, not current.

beats.idea: Descriptions do not establish precise metrics
beats.shows: Unsupported shares, fixed rates and continuity crossed out
beats.template_note: Logical inferences are rejected, not a person's offered payment; show inference icons before crosses and leave ranking awaiting a measure.

beats.idea: Excess demand can reduce purchasing power
beats.shows: Demand outpaces goods; same money buys less
beats.template_note: First separate reserves from a crossed backing pledge; then grow money and demand against unchanged goods, conditionally raising prices and reducing the same-money basket.

beats.idea: Valid payment clears the debt
beats.relation_note: The same outstanding debt changes from ₹100 to ₹0 after payment.
beats.shows: ₹100 handed over; debt falls to ₹0
beats.template_note: Customer gives the ₹100 note; shopkeeper takes it and marks the ₹100 debt settled, leaving ₹0.

beats.idea: Valid special-design coins buy goods
beats.relation_note: Tick the special-design coin when the shopkeeper accepts it as full payment.
beats.shows: Special-design coin accepted; ₹10 item handed back
beats.image_wanted: Indian ₹10 circulation commemorative coin obverse reverse
beats.template_note: Customer hands over one valid ₹10 coin; shopkeeper accepts it with a nod and tick, then hands over the ₹10 item.

beats.idea: Notes scale; coin acceptance has a limit
beats.relation_note: Contrast note payments with a coin-value meter stopping at the ₹1,000 compulsory-acceptance line; above it acceptance is voluntary.
beats.shows: Note stacks grow; coin meter reaches legal limit
beats.template_note: First show two ₹500 notes paying ₹1,000, then three paying ₹1,500. Next count 100 ₹10 coins as their value meter reaches the ₹1,000 red line. Hold coin 101 outside the compulsory stack: the offered total becomes ₹1,010, while the compulsory meter stays capped. Show the shopkeeper's choice above the line, not an automatic cross.

beats.idea: Official recognition, territorial use, circulating commemoratives
beats.shows: Stamped money inside India; commemorative coin buys goods
beats.template_note: Within the territory outline, recognised money passes from payer to recipient beside a debt receipt; then a circulation commemorative coin passes to a shopkeeper like an ordinary coin.

beats.idea: Valid banknotes have no total tender ceiling
nouns: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 law scroll
beats.shows: Valid notes stack upward beside stamped RBI law
beats.template_note: Genuine, valid notes accumulate and a total rises without a stop line; reveal the six named denominations and the stamped RBI Act beside them. This is accumulation, not a coin-limit count.

beats.idea: Compulsory coin acceptance stops at the legal limit
beats.shows: Coin meter stops; extra coins enter optional tray
beats.template_note: Coins build a pile as the meter reaches a red line labelled legally prescribed limit. Show further coins separately with a recipient choice symbol, not an invalidity cross; associate the limit with Coinage Act, 2011.

beats.idea: Tender status is not unrestricted cash permission
beats.shows: Three paired contrasts separate permission, circulation, validity
beats.template_note: These are conceptual contrasts, not counting or payment processes: unlimited note tender versus transaction rules; special design versus established circulation and a separate collector set; coins beyond the limit retaining validity while acceptance becomes voluntary.

beats.idea: After recognition, distinguish denomination and total limit
beats.shows: Recognised notes extend upward; coins meet limit line
beats.template_note: A static matched comparison consolidates the answer: denomination tags on both sides, no total tender ceiling for notes, and a prescribed compulsory-acceptance limit for coins.

beats.idea: Legal tender से fiat होना अनिवार्य नहीं
beats.shows: Bitcoin exception crosses universal-rule arrow
beats.template_note: तार्किक अनिवार्यता का खंडन है, भुगतान ठुकराने की प्रक्रिया नहीं। Legal tender से fiat तक arrow पर ‘must’ रखें; उसे काटें, Bitcoin को नहीं।

beats.idea: Commemorative coins के status और values अलग
beats.shows: Coin group subdivided; metal and collector tags
beats.template_note: Fiat issues के पूरे समूह में बड़ा legal-tender उपसमूह और छोटा non-legal-tender उपसमूह दिखाएँ; proportions संख्यात्मक न हों। नीचे metal और collector value के अलग tags रखें, बिना कीमत या क्रम गढ़े।

beats.idea: Collector sets की condition सुरक्षित रखी जाती है
beats.shows: Mint sells sets; capsules protect pristine coins
beats.image_wanted: Government Mint commemorative proof coin set UNC packaging
beats.template_note: Collector money देता है, mint seller packaged set सौंपता है। फिर proof पर खास finish का close-up और UNC पर ‘Uncirculated’ label दिखाएँ; protective capsule से condition बचने का arrow, daily-payment रास्ता हल्का रखें, बंद नहीं।

beats.idea: Withdrawn coins do not clear the bill
beats.relation_note: Follow rejection with acceptance of a valid coin and an outstanding-balance change.
beats.shows: Old coins rejected; valid coin clears ₹1 bill
beats.image_wanted: Indian 25 paise coin obverse and reverse
beats.template_note: First show four 25 paise coins beside a ₹1 bill and a question mark. On मना, the shopkeeper shakes their head and a cross lands on the coins; outstanding stays ₹1. Then the customer hands over a valid ₹1 coin, the shopkeeper accepts, and outstanding changes from ₹1 to ₹0. On demonetization, cross out the old coins' legal-tender stamp, not their numerical face value.

beats.idea: Coin groups have different tender limits
beats.relation_note: Two separate group-total meters and a rejected below-50-paise group.
beats.shows: Two coin meters stop; smaller coins crossed out
beats.template_note: Open the change box with a question mark. Group ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20 coins into one row; coins accumulate while its combined-value meter rises and stops at the ₹1,000 red line. In a separate row, 50 paise coins accumulate to a ₹10 red line. Show below-50-paise coins in a third row, then cross them on नहीं; do not show them filling a valid-payment meter or returning as change.

book_pictures.title: Current legal limits for coins (Coinage Act, 2011)

beats.idea: Denomination times count gives the limited amount
beats.shows: Coin piles grow; rupee meters reach red limits
beats.template_note: Count 50 ₹20 coins as the amount reaches ₹1,000; cross out only the mistaken ‘1,000 coins’ counter label. Then count 20 fifty-paise coins as the amount reaches ₹10. Keep denomination, count and total in separate slots.

beats.idea: Different denominations need different status checks
beats.shows: Separated coins: capped tender versus crossed tender badge
beats.image_wanted: Indian 50 paise coin 25 paise coin commemorative coin
beats.template_note: Move 50-paise and 25-paise coins from a box into matching comparison slots. Attach ₹10 limit to the first; cross the tender badge, not the coin, on the second. Then show commemorative coins with varied status badges and an unresolved count question; ‘most’ produces no numerical tally.

beats.idea: Payment limits and collectible value do not determine status
beats.shows: Over-limit pile keeps status; priced coin stays demonetized
beats.template_note: Increase a valid-coin payment pile beyond its amount limit while leaving the individual coin’s tender badge unchanged. In a parallel panel attach a collector price tag to a 25-paise coin; its crossed tender badge remains crossed. No purchase or change-giving is narrated.

beats.idea: Calculate amount, then check limit and status
beats.shows: Denomination times count, then limit and status checks
beats.template_note: Animate denomination and coin count entering multiplication; move the resulting amount to a limit comparison, then check the coin’s tender-status badge against the book table. Reuse the earlier coin examples without inventing new amounts.

beats.idea: Payment appearance does not identify issuer
beats.shows: Bitcoin phone; government question; separate legal-status scroll
beats.template_note: Payment is a contextual display, not a narrated transaction.

beats.idea: Legal tender exception, network issuance and market price
beats.shows: 2024 recognition; mining creates bitcoin; market sets price
beats.template_note: Show network-rule validation producing new bitcoin; separately animate demand-supply moving its price. Cross the government fixed-value promise document at नहीं।

beats.idea: Compulsion removed, ownership and voluntary payment retained
beats.shows: Compulsion crossed; wallet ticked; consenting pair exchanges bitcoin
beats.template_note: At हटी cross only compulsory acceptance; retain ownership tick. Both parties nod at राज़ी, then Bitcoin transfers from buyer wallet to seller wallet.

beats.idea: Legal-status change does not change issuer
beats.shows: Legal scroll changes; network stays; government issuer crossed
beats.template_note: Conceptual comparison of legal status and issuer, not a transaction.

beats.idea: Ask three separate monetary-status questions
beats.shows: Issuer, wallet, handshake and law with question marks
beats.template_note: Acceptance is a classification question here, not an act of accepting payment.

beats.idea: One coin, two roles
beats.shows: Same coin: payment versus collection, question mark
beats.image_wanted: Indian ₹100 silver commemorative coin denomination visible
beats.template_note: Introduces two roles and a question, not a transaction.

beats.idea: Face value differs from market price
beats.shows: Same coin; ₹100 debt versus several-thousand price
beats.image_wanted: Indian ₹100 silver commemorative coin denomination visible
beats.template_note: Compares values without enacting a sale.

beats.idea: Collector premium leaves denomination unchanged
beats.shows: Silver, condition, collectability raise offer; ₹100 unchanged
beats.image_wanted: Indian ₹100 silver commemorative coin surface detail
beats.template_note: Collector examines silver, condition and collection appeal, then hands seller the agreed higher payment; ₹100 on coin remains visible. No exact price invented.

beats.idea: Collector price is not a payment rule
beats.shows: Collector-price links to debt and legal-limit crossed
beats.template_note: Rejects equivalence, not a person’s tender; cross only the links. No counting or numerical limit is narrated.

beats.idea: Payment denomination; collection agreed price
beats.shows: Payment: ₹100 coin; collection: handshake price tag
beats.image_wanted: Indian ₹100 silver commemorative coin denomination visible
beats.template_note: Recaps the comparison; handshake symbolizes agreement rather than enacting payment.

beats.idea: Cheque transfers existing deposits, subject to funds
beats.shows: Cheque clears; student balance falls, college receives ₹1,000
beats.template_note: Write ₹1,000 cheque, submit to bank, then show student balance ₹2,000 becoming ₹1,000 and college receiving ₹1,000. Separate insufficient-funds branch leaves the fee bill unpaid.

beats.idea: Credit pays fees but creates repayment debt
beats.shows: Issuer pays college; student debt rises to ₹1,000
beats.template_note: Animate issuer payment ₹1,000 to college; then change student's debt to issuer from ₹0 to ₹1,000, excluding charges. Keep deposit account outside the payment path; do not show repayment occurring.

beats.idea: Payment instruments currency नहीं हैं
beats.shows: Cheque–card pathways; college tick, legal-status inference crossed
beats.template_note: Cheque से deposit ledger तक instruction arrow; credit card से credit limit तक access arrow। College clerk दोनों स्वीकार करे; acceptance tick से fiat/legal-tender stamp तक निकला inference arrow cross हो, instruments स्वयं नहीं।

beats.idea: तीन अलग सवाल; dollar माँग का प्रश्न
beats.shows: Three separate tiles; dollar question, gold link crossed
beats.template_note: Value, legal status और payment method का स्थिर पृथक्करण और अगले विषय का प्रश्न है; कोई payment process नहीं।
